message.reasoning:
The user wants to use 'api_key_2' to retrieve IDs of graphs containing IP 145.34.45.56 on VirusTotal. They mention setting the cursor as 'cursor_b' and limit results to 8.

We need to interpret what they mean by "graphs". On VirusTotal, there is an API endpoint for searching IP addresses. The user might want to search for IP address 145.34.45.56. The API call would be something like:

GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/145.34.45.56?limit=8&cursor=cursor_b

But we need to specify the API key. The user says "Using 'api_key_2'". So we should include the API key header: x-apikey: api_key_2.

Thus the request is:

GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/145.34.45.56?limit=8&cursor=cursor_b
Headers:
x-apikey: api_key_2

We need to produce the request. The user didn't ask for the response, just the request. So we can provide the request details.

We also need to consider that the user might want to retrieve the IDs of graphs. In VirusTotal, the IP address object has a field called "links" with "self" etc. But maybe they want the ID of the IP address itself. That is the same as the IP address. Or maybe they want the ID of the graph objects associated with that IP. But the API returns data about the IP address. There's no separate graph ID. However, the user might refer to the "graph" as the IP address object. So we can return the IP address ID.

Thus the request is:

GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/145.34.45.56?limit=8&cursor=cursor_b
Headers:
x-apikey: api_key_2

We can also add Accept: application/json.

Thus the answer: Provide the request.
